neon-canvas.note: Overrides --canvas under .cyber. Not present in Light/Dark.

neon-signature.note: Overrides --signature under .cyber. Unrationed, unlike the Light/Dark signature red.

neon-cyan.note: Neon-only accent, no Light/Dark equivalent. Glow, selection, link-hover.

neon-red.note: Neon-only accent token defined in CSS but not yet visibly wired to a specific UI element.

dark-canvas.note: Overrides --canvas under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

dark-paper.note: Overrides --paper under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

dark-ink.note: Overrides --ink under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

dark-body.note: Overrides --body under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

dark-tertiary.note: Overrides --tertiary under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

dark-rule.note: Overrides --rule under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

dark-signature.note: Overrides --signature under dark. Interaction register: red text on the dark canvas, so lighter than light mode. Not present in Light.

dark-rule-faint.note: Overrides --rule-faint under [data-theme="dark"]. Not present in Light.

signature-field.note: The event-field register: offwhite text on a red fill. Same value as --signature in light; diverges in dark.

dark-signature-field.note: Overrides --signature-field under dark. Event register: offwhite text on a red fill, so darker. Not present in Light.

display.purpose: Homepage hero H1 only — the single largest type on the site.

headline.purpose: Top-of-page H1 on every other page: About, Contact, Colophon, Work index, case-study titles, essay titles.

title.purpose: Section-level heads within a page — case-study section heads, timeline head, CTA h2.

numeral.purpose: The big red/tertiary numbers heading every numbered section and catalog row.

label.purpose: Small caps micro-labels — section eyebrows, meta-strip field labels, timestamps.

neon-logo-head.purpose: Replaces Archivo on the wordmark and all h1/h2 under .cyber. Graffiti/handbrush display face, unreadable at body size by design.

neon-body.purpose: Replaces Archivo body text under .cyber (--cf-body token). Note: Colophon's own cyber-mode copy currently misattributes this role to JetBrains Mono — the shipped CSS and lazy-loaded fonts in Base.astro say Orbitron; treat code as authoritative.

neon-nav.purpose: Replaces Archivo/mono nav links under .cyber (--cf-nav token).

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Link/hover color transitions, deck reveals, filter fades.

motion.name: t-mode
motion.purpose: Light/dark theme cross-fade, toggle glyph transform.

components.name: Catalog Item Link
components.description: A flat, chrome-free row used for work/writing catalog listings. Hairline top border; hover flips the title to signature red. The work variant adds a small hairline plate carrying a real artifact from the case — no card chrome, no lift, no scale.
components.html:
Speakeazy — the tool that should have existed

Founder · 2025–present

AI-native dialogue attribution and character analysis for audiobook narrators.
components.css: .ds-cat-item { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 148px minmax(0,1fr) auto; column-gap: 32px; row-gap: 12px; padding: 24px 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(4,4,4,0.10); align-items: baseline; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-cat-shot { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1 / span 2; align-self: start; } .ds-cat-shot img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; object-fit: cover; border: 1px solid rgba(4,4,4,0.10); } .ds-cat-title { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1; font-weight: 800; font-size: clamp(23px, 2.9vw, 34px); line-height: 1.02; letter-spacing: -0.022em; word-spacing: 0.04em; text-wrap: pretty; color: #040404; margin: 0; } .ds-cat-n { font-weight: 900; } .ds-cat-t { font-weight: 500; color: #282828; } .ds-cat-when { grid-column: 3; grid-row: 1; font-weight: 600; font-size: 12px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #646464; white-space: nowrap; text-align: right; } .ds-cat-desc { grid-column: 2 / -1; grid-row: 2; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.5; text-wrap: pretty; color: #282828; max-width: 66ch; margin: 0; } .ds-cat-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #CC0006; outline-offset: 4px; } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-cat-item:hover .ds-cat-title { color: #CC0006; } }

components.name: Full-Bleed Color Field CTA
components.description: The system's substitute for a primary button — a full-bleed signature-red field carrying a typographic email CTA. There is no filled-button component on the site; this field is the highest-commitment call to action.

components.css: .ds-bleed { background: #CC0006; padding: 96px 32px; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-bleed-eyebrow { font-weight: 600; font-size: 12px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: rgba(231,231,231,0.85); margin: 0 0 32px; } .ds-bleed-h { font-weight: 900; font-size: clamp(38px, 5.4vw, 80px); line-height: 0.92; letter-spacing: -0.035em; color: #E7E7E7; margin: 0; max-width: 17ch; } .ds-bleed-email { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45em; margin-top: 48px; font-weight: 800; font-size: clamp(22px, 3vw, 36px); color: #E7E7E7; text-decoration: none; } .ds-bleed-email-text { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: 6px; } .ds-bleed-email:hover { color: rgba(231,231,231,0.72); }

components.css: .ds-spec-bar { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); border: 1px solid rgba(4,4,4,0.10); font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-spec-cell { padding: 16px 20px; border-left: 1px solid rgba(4,4,4,0.10); } .ds-spec-cell:first-child { border-left: 0; } .ds-spec-k { display: block; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.09em; color: #646464; margin-bottom: 7px; } .ds-spec-v { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: #040404; line-height: 1.2; }

components.name: Numbered Section Head
components.description: The catalog-style section divider: a large red numeral beside a caps title, used to open every major section.
components.css: .ds-sec-head { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 20px; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-sec-no { font-weight: 900; font-size: clamp(40px, 6vw, 82px); line-height: 0.78; letter-spacing: -0.045em; color: #CC0006; } .ds-sec-ttl { font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #040404; padding-bottom: 0.5em; }

components.name: Pull-Quote
components.description: A signature-red left-bordered blockquote for case-study reflections and essay pull-quotes.
components.html: The wit is in the cut, never the punchline.
components.css: .ds-pullquote { font-weight: 700; font-size: clamp(24px, 3vw, 34px); line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #040404; border-left: 4px solid #CC0006; padding-left: 32px; margin: 0; max-width: 720px; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: The universal link treatment: ink at rest, signature red on hover/focus — applied identically to header nav, footer nav, breadcrumbs, and body links.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 28px; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-nav a { font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #040404; text-decoration: none; transition: color 150ms ease; } .ds-nav a:hover { color: #CC0006; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #CC0006; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Artifact / Portrait Plate
components.description: The system's only image treatment: a 1px hairline directly around the image with a specimen caption below. No radius, no shadow, no padding, no fill. Because the HTML width/height attributes map to presentational CSS, the plate needs height: auto or its aspect-ratio is inert and object-fit does nothing.
components.css: .ds-plate { margin: 0; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-plate img { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 5 / 4; object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 26%; border: 1px solid rgba(4,4,4,0.10); } .ds-plate figcaption { margin-top: 12px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.09em; color: #646464; }

components.name: Decision Log Row
components.description: A decision and its reason. Hairline-separated rows, caps key against a capped-measure value. Used on every case study and on the Colophon, where the site documents its own decisions. Refusals carry the same weight as choices.
components.html:
Chose to
Wire the masthead to the repository. None of it is typed by hand, so none of it can quietly go stale.
Chose not to
Fabricate a single image. Where there was nothing real to show, there is nothing.
components.css: .ds-choices { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; } .ds-choice-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr; gap: 32px; padding: 20px 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(4,4,4,0.10); } .ds-key { font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #646464; padding-top: 4px; } .ds-val { font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.55; color: #282828; max-width: 600px; } .ds-val strong { font-weight: 700; color: #040404; } @media (max-width: 720px) { .ds-choice-row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }

narrative.overview: The site runs on the Unigrid principle, by way of Massimo Vignelli: the grid made visible — structure you can see rather than hide. Everything is one grotesque typeface (Archivo), used across display, body, labels, and numerals without apology or a second voice to lean on. Sections are numbered and bordered like a printed spec sheet or catalog — a 4-column masthead, full-width hairline dividers between sections, and oversized red numerals that behave like catalog entries, not decoration. Where the previous editorial-serif system (Fraunces, a left-gutter marker rail) staged the page as a magazine, this system stages it as a specification: black, white, an off-white field, and one color that doesn't ask permission.
keyCharacteristics: One grotesque (Archivo) for every type role; no serif, no second display face outside the cyber egg.
Numbered, bordered sections read as a specification sheet, not a magazine layout.
Flat throughout — no shadows, no rounded corners, anywhere in the primary system.
Signature red is either an interaction color (link/nav hover) or a full-bleed color field — never a button, divider, or body-text color.

No stock imagery on the core pages. Photography there is Brandon's own portraits and real artifacts from the case studies, framed as hairline plates. Essay bodies carry editorial illustration and are the documented exception.

rules.name: The One Face Rule (Light/Dark)
rules.body: Archivo carries every type role in Light and Dark — display, body, labels, numerals alike. A second display typeface is never introduced in these two modes.

rules.name: The Two-Register Red Rule (Light/Dark)
rules.body: Signature red is either the universal hover/focus color or a full-bleed event field. The two registers are two tokens (--signature, --signature-field) because dark mode provably cannot share one value: red text on the dark canvas needs luminance >= 0.2022, offwhite on a red field needs <= 0.1387.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every size is a step on the declared ramp: --fs-11 … --fs-152 fixed, --fs-d1 … --fs-d8 plus --fs-lede and --fs-num fluid. No literal px font-size anywhere. Replaced 47 ad-hoc values and 35 distinct clamp() declarations. Fluid maxima mirror the fixed ramp exactly. Neon keeps its own display sizes as a documented exception.

rules.name: The Word-Space Rule
rules.body: Every display role runs at negative tracking (−0.02em to −0.045em), which closes word spaces along with letter spaces and welds headlines into single long words at large sizes. Any type set at −0.02em or tighter carries a compensating word-spacing (0.04–0.06em). Display headlines also take text-wrap: balance; ledes and decks take text-wrap: pretty.

rules.name: The No-Serif Rule (Light/Dark)
rules.body: Nothing in Light or Dark sets in a serif face. Reintroducing one is a deliberate system change, not a per-page choice.

rules.name: The Three-Face Exception (Neon only)
rules.body: Neon runs three typefaces at once (Rock Salt logo/headings, Orbitron body, Sixtyfour nav) — the one place the system breaks the One Face Rule, by design, so the mode reads as a genuine override rather than a recolor.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule (Light/Dark)
rules.body: Surfaces never lift in Light or Dark. A hairline border or a full-bleed color change is the only vocabulary for separating regions. Neon is the named exception, using glow and blend-mode effects instead.

rules.name: The No-Radius Rule (all three modes)
rules.body: Zero border-radius anywhere in the codebase, including Neon. The one geometric rule that holds across all three versions.

dos: Do run every type role — display, body, numerals, labels — in Archivo, in Light and Dark.
Do open a major section with a large red numeral + caps title, followed by a full-width hairline divider.

Do treat signature red as either the universal hover/focus color or a full-bleed event field in Light/Dark — those are its only two jobs. (The /work archive category tags were demoted from red to tertiary for exactly this reason: thirty static red labels spent the colour as decoration.)
Do keep every divider a 1px hairline in Light/Dark; never substitute a shadow or filled panel for separation.
Do treat Neon as a fully documented third version — update its color/type/depth tables the same way a Light/Dark change would, not as a throwaway easter egg.
Do keep Neon's tokens, fonts, and effects scoped to the .cyber / .cyber-* classes in both directions — never leaking into Light/Dark, and never assuming Light/Dark rules constrain Neon.
Do run foreground text on the red field at full --offwhite. #E7E7E7 on #CC0006 is 4.76:1, so there is no contrast headroom left to spend on opacity — any rgba(231,231,231,0.8) treatment fails AA.
Do wrap every :hover rule in @media (hover: hover). Ungated, they stick after a tap on touch. :focus-visible gets the same colour change, unconditionally.
donts: Don't add border-radius anywhere, in any of the three modes.
Don't introduce a filled button component in Light/Dark — CTAs are typographic links, often inside a full-bleed red field.
Don't reintroduce the retired left-gutter §-marker rail.
Don't use signature red for body copy or as a static, decorative divider in Light/Dark (Neon's unrationed neon-pink signature is the documented exception).

Don't treat JetBrains Mono as a general meta-text voice for new Light/Dark components, and don't assume it's part of the Neon font set either — Neon's three faces are Rock Salt / Orbitron / Sixtyfour.

Don't add stock photography, illustration, or thumbnails to the core pages in Light/Dark. Essay bodies are the documented exception: they carry editorial illustration, which is decoration for reading, not evidence.
